synthesis.executiveSummary: Two north stars govern this backlog: (1) full C++ decomp of Fable.exe, and (2) injection-first "own the whole pipeline" authoring. On decomp, the BSim symbol-port is mature (Fable.exe at 80.14% named, 49,081/49,082 functions decompile clean) so bar #1 (full pseudo-C) is a grind that is already running; the real gate on bar #2 (buildable source) and the entire lift-harness chain is one blocked prerequisite: VC7.1/MSVC 2003 is not installed. Obtaining it is a small user action that unblocks 3+ items and the whole functional-rebuild horizon. On authoring, the pipeline is far more built than the raw gap count suggests: anim writer, mesh compose (type-1 + type-5 skinned), and the animation decoder are already SHIPPED/CLOSED and should not be re-litigated. The dominant pattern is BUILT-but-untested: ~35 live-test items are cheap value-conversion, and many share a single game-launch session (save edit, Profile.bin, text.big, frontend.bin, .lut/.lug audio, custom region/card/terrain). The two highest-leverage coding tasks that convert the most surface at once are the LZO1X-1 encoder (last gate on texture authoring, sources available) and the C3DMesh2::LoadBinary geometry walk port (unblocks 5 deduped mesh/Blender items at once). Several fix-class defects share root causes: quest-card def-append failure (4 duplicate entries, has a known overwrite workaround), save_edit childhood-intro corruption, and silent swapped-audio — all need runtime/decomp RE. Biggest levers: install VC7.1, run the batched live-test session, port the geometry walk, port the LZO encoder, and run the pending container/round-trip write gates that let native writers ship.
